title: HTML Exercises
description: Practice every HTML lesson with multiple-choice questions, output prediction, find-the-error tasks and small coding tasks you can check in the playground.

exercises.question: Write a complete HTML document whose tab title is "About me", with a level-one heading containing your name and one paragraph describing what you want to build.
exercises.explanation: A valid document starts with the doctype, has an html element with a lang attribute, a head with charset and title, and a body with the visible content.
exercises.solutionCode:
Ada Lovelace

I want to build a small website for my garden club.
checklist: There is exactly one h1 containing a name
There is a paragraph element with a sentence inside

exercises.question: In `Contact us`, which part is the *content* of the element?
exercises.explanation: The content is everything between the opening and closing tags: the text "Contact us". `href="/contact"` is an attribute and `<a>` is the opening tag.

exercises.question:
You open your page and the browser shows `

Hello

` as literal text instead of a heading. What is the most likely cause?
exercises.explanation: When the file is saved as .txt the browser treats it as plain text and shows the tags. Saving it with the .html extension fixes it.
options: The browser does not support HTML
The file was saved with a .txt extension
The heading needs a class attribute

exercises.question: How many list items does the browser display?
exercises.explanation: The second item is inside a comment, so it is not rendered. Only Milk and Eggs are displayed.

exercises.question: This snippet is invalid HTML. What is wrong?
exercises.explanation: The elements overlap: `` is opened inside `` but `` is closed first. The inner element must be closed before the outer one: `very important`.
options: The closing tags are in the wrong order (overlapping elements)
The paragraph is missing a class

exercises.explanation:

exercises.question: The tooltip on this link shows only the word "Visit". Why?
exercises.explanation: The attribute value is not quoted, so it ends at the first space. `the` and `site` become meaningless extra attributes. Quote the value: `title="Visit the site"`.
options: The attribute value is unquoted, so it stops at the first space
The link text is too short

exercises.question: `<input disabled="false">` produces an enabled input.
exercises.explanation: Boolean attributes are true whenever they are present, whatever the value. The only way to enable the input is to remove the attribute.

exercises.question: A page has an `<h1>` followed by an `<h2>` and then an `<h4>`. What is wrong with the outline?
exercises.explanation: Heading levels should not skip downwards. After an `<h2>`, the next lower level is `<h3>`; jumping to `<h4>` leaves a gap in the outline.
options: It skips a level from h2 to h4
A page may only use h1 and h2

exercises.question: What does the browser display for this paragraph?
exercises.explanation: Whitespace collapses inside a paragraph: all the spaces and line breaks become single spaces, giving "one two three" on one line.
options: Three words on three separate lines
"one" then a blank line then "two three"
The extra spaces are preserved exactly

exercises.question: A warning sentence must be conveyed as important to screen-reader users as well as sighted users. Which element should wrap it?
exercises.explanation: `<strong>` carries the meaning of importance; `<b>` and a styled `<span>` only change appearance, and `<mark>` means highlighted relevance.

exercises.question: A page at `/blog/2026/post.html` needs to link to `/blog/index.html`. Using a relative path that goes up one folder, the href is `___`.
exercises.explanation: `../` moves from the `2026` folder up to `blog`, so `../index.html` resolves to `/blog/index.html`.

exercises.question: To open a link in a new tab you add the attribute `target="___"`.
exercises.explanation: `target="_blank"` opens the destination in a new browsing context; pair it with `rel="noopener"`.

exercises.question: A purely decorative divider image sits between two sections. What should its alt attribute be?
exercises.explanation: Decorative images get an empty alt (`alt=""`) so screen readers skip them. Omitting the attribute makes screen readers read the file name.

exercises.question: This image causes the layout to jump when it loads and is announced badly by screen readers. Which two attributes are missing?
exercises.explanation: Without `width` and `height` the browser cannot reserve space, and without `alt` screen readers announce the file name. Add `alt`, `width` and `height`.

exercises.question: Build an accessible table of three programming languages and their first release year. Include a caption, a header row with scope attributes and the three data rows.
exercises.explanation: An accessible data table has a caption, header cells with scope="col" in a thead, and data rows in a tbody.
exercises.solutionCode:
Programming languages and their first release
Language First released
Python1991
Java1995
Go2009
checklist: Header cells use th with scope="col"
Headers are inside thead and data rows inside tbody
Every row has exactly two cells

exercises.question: The second row of this table renders with a cell hanging outside the grid. What is wrong?
exercises.explanation: The header cell spans two columns, so the table is two columns wide, but the data row has three cells. Remove one cell or change the colspan.
options: The data row has more cells than the table has columns

exercises.question: This nested list is invalid HTML. Why?
exercises.explanation: A `<ul>` may only contain `<li>` children. The inner list must go inside the "Fruit" list item, after its text, not between two `<li>` elements.
options: Nested lists are not allowed in HTML
The inner `<ul>` is a direct child of the outer `<ul>` instead of being inside an `<li>`
The outer list should be an `<ol>`

exercises.question: Which element pair is designed for a glossary of terms and their definitions?
exercises.explanation: Description lists pair `<dt>` terms with `<dd>` descriptions inside a `<dl>`.

exercises.question: Which snippet correctly connects the label to the input?
exercises.explanation: The label's `for` must match the input's `id`. Matching the `name` or the placeholder does not create the connection.

exercises.question: A form that creates a new user account should use `method="get"` so the data appears in the URL.
exercises.explanation: Actions that change data or carry private information should use POST. GET puts the values in the URL, where they are logged and bookmarkable, which is wrong for passwords and sign-ups.

exercises.question: A pizza order lets customers choose exactly one size. Which input type should the size options use?
exercises.explanation: Radio buttons sharing the same name allow exactly one choice. Checkboxes allow several, and text inputs would not restrict the answer.

exercises.question: To stop the browser from submitting a form while a field is empty, add the boolean attribute `___` to that field.
exercises.explanation: `required` makes the browser block submission and show a message until the field has a value.

exercises.question: A blog post that would make sense on its own in an RSS feed should be wrapped in which element?
exercises.explanation: `<article>` is for self-contained content that can stand alone; `<section>` groups related content within a page and `<aside>` is for tangential content.

exercises.question: A screen-reader user cannot jump to the main content of this page. What is missing?
exercises.explanation: There is no `<main>` landmark. Replace the content `<div>` with `<main>` so assistive technology can jump straight to it.
options: The content is in a `<div>` instead of a `<main>` landmark

exercises.question: Modern browsers allow a video to autoplay with sound as long as the `autoplay` attribute is present.
exercises.explanation: Browsers block autoplay with sound. Autoplay only works when the video is muted, which is why background clips use autoplay together with muted.

exercises.question: A `<video>` lists a WebM `<source>` followed by an MP4 `<source>`. A browser that supports both will play…
exercises.explanation: The browser plays the first source it supports, in document order, so the WebM file is used. Put the preferred format first.
options: The MP4, because it is the fallback
The WebM, because it is listed first
Neither, because two sources are not allowed

exercises.question: What does this script print?
exercises.explanation: `setItem` stores the string "3". After `removeItem`, `getItem` returns null for the missing key.

exercises.question: Which method opens a `<dialog>` as a modal that traps focus and shows a backdrop?
exercises.explanation: `showModal()` opens the dialog modally with a backdrop and focus trapping; `show()` opens it as a non-modal dialog.

exercises.question: Which title is the best choice for a page about balcony tomato growing on the site "Garden Notes"?
exercises.explanation: Specific topic first, site name last, around 50–60 characters. "Home" and the bare site name say nothing about the page, and keyword lists read as spam.
options: `Growing Tomatoes on a Balcony – Garden Notes`
`tomatoes tomato growing balcony tomatoes guide tips`

exercises.question: Complete the head of this page with a unique title, a meta description, the viewport tag, a canonical link and an Open Graph title.
exercises.explanation: A search-friendly head has charset, viewport, a specific title, a meta description, a canonical URL and Open Graph tags for sharing.
exercises.solutionCode: Herbs for beginners
checklist: A viewport meta tag is present
The title names the topic and is under 60 characters
A meta description of 120–160 characters is present
A canonical link points to the page's preferred URL
An og:title meta tag is present
